title: Pixel-budget ladder extended to 8 equal levels in two domains not used for the ordering, and the cross-domain ordering of that knob's span re-estimated with a bootstrap lower bound
why: Section 7.3's ordering claim rests on a unit set in which (a) two of the design's six knobs have no proxy and (b) the MTDC row is thin (the appendix itself notes that only ONE level falls inside the 1.10x travel band). Reviewers asked for the equal-level ladder to be extended into genuinely unused domains.
machine: A800, SINGLE CARD, GPU1 only (GPU0 belongs to another session and is never touched)

design.knob: VLM·pixel budget (the knob whose ladder the appendix itself calls thin in MTDC)
design.knob_note: This round drives ONE knob. The appendix's own thin-row complaint is about this ladder (the 1.10x travel band contains a single level in MTDC), and the knob is the only one whose eight levels were already pre-registered by the paper itself in the matched-travel ladder - so re-using them keeps the new domains comparable to the published ones.
design.levels_note: 11 levels = the 5 labels the released res_ctrl__q32 ladders carry ({0,200000,400000,800000} plus native, with 1048576 folded into 0 by the paper's own rule) UNION the 8 matched-travel values. The union is deliberate: the ordering units of F.2/M.37 are built FROM res_ctrl__*, so a new domain can only be ADDED to that unit set if it carries the same budget labels - otherwise it can only be reported descriptively, which does not answer the ordering question. 11 >= 8 also satisfies the equal-level requirement. Resize convention pinned by per-row inversion of the released ladders: budget=0 => native, no resize; otherwise s=sqrt(budget/(W*H)) only when the image exceeds the budget, then each side is floored to a multiple of 28 (Qwen smart_resize factor 28). Anchored on a real row: 902x409 at budget 200000 -> the released eff is 644x280, which is exactly floor(902*s/28)*28 x floor(409*s/28)*28.

mtdc.role: new (not previously used for the ordering)

gwhd.role: new (not previously used for the ordering)
gwhd.pool: GlobalWheatHeadDataset2021 test split (1,381 items) extracted from parquet

design.sampling: deterministic: sort the pool by item, then draw 250 indices with random.Random(20261002).sample; the drawn list is frozen in /root/p1d/data/sample_<domain>.csv. Items whose gt is 0 ARE KEPT (they are part of the domain); their counts are reported. Nothing is dropped or added after seeing a prediction.
design.starts_note: three fresh service starts, exactly as the earlier ladder runs
design.calls_check: 2 domains x 11 levels x 250 items x 3 starts = 16500
design.serve: /root/pf_serve_awq4bit_8013.sh (Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct-AWQ, port 8013, single card, gmem 0.85, max-model-len 8192, max-num-seqs 24, limit-mm-per-prompt {image:1}, mm-processor max_pixels 1048576 / min_pixels 3136)
design.call_params: temperature 0, max_tokens 128, retries 5, workers 4 - inherited VERBATIM from the frozen probe /root/pf_p0_probe.py (call_img / b64_of / parse are imported, never retyped)

frozen_inputs.published_comparator: analysis/data/pod_mirror/res_ctrl__q32/res_ctrl_{st_a,ucf,visdrone}.csv (the paper's own pixel-budget ladders, same 8 budgets, same served model) - released in the reproduction package

estimator.per_level: dev(level) = 100 * (sum(pred) - sum(gt)) / sum(gt), pooled over THAT LEVEL'S OWN items (the caliber locked by the G0 self-check; never the common-item intersection)
estimator.span: max(dev over the eight levels) - min(dev over the eight levels)
estimator.ordering: Spearman rank correlation over the per-domain spans of this knob, published domains + new domains together
estimator.bootstrap: item-level resample within each domain, B = 2000, seed 20261002, report the 2.5th percentile of the Spearman as the lower bound

criteria.statement: every (domain x level x start) cell holds all 250 items; checked per cell, not sampled
criteria.abort: if a cell is short, mark THAT CELL not evaluable, keep going, and report the count; never pad

criteria.statement: both domains carry all eight levels (no gaps)
criteria.abort: a domain with fewer than eight levels is reported as NOT COVERED and is excluded from the ordering; interpolation to fill a level is forbidden

criteria.statement: report, per domain, the eight level devs and the span

recompute the three published domains' spans for this knob from the released ladders (res_ctrl__q32/res_ctrl_{st_a,ucf,visdrone}.csv), using ONLY the same eight budgets (the released ladders also carry a native=0 row, which is excluded); this is the estimator gate - if my dev/span does not reproduce the published per-domain values and their ordering, nothing below is comparable
criteria.decision_rule: PASS if the recomputed per-domain spans rank-order identically to the published ordering (Spearman = 1.00) and the item-level bootstrap (B=2000, seed 20261002) lower bound on that Spearman is >= 0.80

criteria.statement: with the two new domains added, report the five-domain span vector and check whether each new span falls inside [0.5x, 2.0x] of the median of the three published spans
criteria.decision_rule: PASS if both new spans are inside that band; otherwise report NOT PASSED and say which domain fell outside. The band is stated here, before the run, so that a large or a tiny new span is a finding rather than a re-drawn target
criteria.why_the_band: the knob's span is claimed to be a property of the knob, so a new domain should land in the same order of magnitude as the domains already measured; a factor of two either way is the loosest band that still excludes the degenerate readings (a floor effect or a sign flip) that the same test produced in the detector/density knobs

criteria.statement: no cell may have parse_ok < 95% without being reported as not evaluable; the served model and the probe md5 must match the frozen values or the run aborts

dual_direction: Both outcomes are reportable. If the ordering does not reproduce, that is the finding: the appendix's own note says the MTDC row was thin, and a thin row is exactly what a new domain can falsify.
caliber_red_lines: Single card via CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1; GPU0 belongs to another session and is never touched; /root/cvpr_exp is never entered.
The budget is applied client-side; the serve-side mm-processor kwargs stay at their frozen values, so the only thing that moves between levels is the pixel budget.
No interpolation to reach eight levels, and no proxy for a domain that cannot be prepared.
Never machine-level pkill: only PIDs recorded by this run's own PID file, each verified to carry --port 8013 in /proc/<pid>/cmdline (NUL-safe).

outputs.csv: P1D_<domain>_b<budget>_s<start>.csv (schema identical to the published res_ctrl files)
outputs.release: this criteria file (md5-frozen) + the runner + the two per-item ladders

appendices.A1_C4a_comparator_budget_mismatch: 事前（尚未跑任何调用）核对放行的 res_ctrl__q32 三件时发现：它们携带的 budget 集合是 {0,200000,400000,800000,1048576}（0 = native），与本轮冻结的 8 档 matched-travel 阶梯**只有一个值（1048576）重合** ⇒ C4a 不可能按『同一组 8 档』算。处置：C4a 如实记为 NOT COMPUTABLE at the eight-level caliber，并**只**按放行件自己的 5 个值描述性报出三域 span（不做跨阶梯比较）；因此新域与已发表域的可比性**限定为同仪器/同模型/同几何**，不声称同档位网格。不影响 C1/C2/C3/C4b/C5。
appendices.A1_union_of_level_labels: PRE-RUN CHANGE (2026-10-02, final): the levels are the UNION of the released res_ctrl__q32 labels {0,200000,400000,800000,native} and the 8 matched-travel values, with 1048576 folded into 0 => 11 labels. Reason: the purpose of P1-D is to ADD the two new domains to the F.2/M.37 ordering unit set, whose budget units are built from res_ctrl__*; a level set that overlaps that set in only one value cannot be added, only reported alongside. With the union, C4a is computable again: it recomputes the three published domains on the FIVE COMMON labels (0/200000/400000/800000 + native) and requires the same ordering with a bootstrap lower bound >= 0.80. Budget therefore becomes 16,500 calls.
appendices.A3_resize_convention: PRE-RUN FIX: the probe originally scaled by round(W*s), which does NOT reproduce the released ladders (902x409 at budget 200000 gives 664x301 by round, but the released file records 644x280). The released convention is floor-to-multiple-of-28, and budget=0 means native with no resize. The probe now implements exactly that, so the new domains' eff_w/eff_h are on the same ruler as the published ones.
appendices.A2_workers_decision: PRE-RUN DECISION (2026-10-02, taken before the full run): smoke 20 items w4 = 109.1 items/min, vLLM 'Running: 4, Waiting: 0'. Concurrency pilot, same card/level/domain, 200 items each: workers=4 -> 126.3 items/min; workers=12 -> 133.3 items/min (Running: 12, Waiting: 0). w12 is only +5.5%, which the rule written before the pilot does not count as 'materially higher', and it doubles in-flight KV pressure; the rule therefore keeps workers=4. The full run uses workers=4 throughout.
